content.title: About
content.content: Italian dressing is a classic sauce made from vinegar, vegetable oil, spices and herbs such as oregano, basil and garlic. It is commonly used to dress salads, marinate vegetables, and add flavor to Italian‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional recipe balances wine vinegar and olive oil in a 1:3 ratio.
Many variations exist, adding lemon juice, honey or mustard.
Italian dressing is often served in restaurants alongside bread for dipping.
The herbs used provide antioxidant benefits.
In the United States the dressing is frequently sold in low‑sugar bottles.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olive oil supplies monounsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and vinegar deliver antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike many ready‑made sauces, Italian dressing typically contains little sugar, which is beneficial for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Herbs add modest amounts of vitamin K, vitamin C and iron.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to olive oil, vinegar or the spices used.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of vinegar can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Commercial versions may contain added salt; low‑sodium options are recommended for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use Italian dressing to dress green or vegetable salads, marinate chicken, fish or vegetables, and as a sauce for pasta and pizza. It can also be stirred into soups for a bright flavor boost.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator. Once opened, it usually keeps for 1–2 months. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
